name: deeply nested / huge / null value_json is stored verbatim without crashing
description: Adversarial value_json robustness probe. Three measurement facts on distinct instants carry hostile-but-valid value_json: (1) deeply nested object with arrays and unicode; (2) a measurement with value_json explicitly null (parse_extraction keeps null when value_json is not a dict); (3) a large flat object. The pipeline stores value_json as-is into a jsonb column — no shape validation beyond 'is it a dict'. This pins that schema-valid-but-degenerate value_json persists cleanly (all three active, accumulating as a time-series), proving value_json is opaque to the pipeline and cannot crash the upsert. Note the open risk this DOCUMENTS: value_json size is unbounded server-side (no length guard in extraction.parse_extraction), so a model could write arbitrarily large jsonb blobs — same family as H1's unbounded-text gap.
xfail: THREE accepted gaps. (1) ACCEPTED, on measurement. assert_fact has no `kind` field, and none of this scenario's predicates is declared in the tier-1 registry, so `_fact_kind` falls back to the subject type's default (`attribute` for a Person). An attribute holds a second value for review, so what was a measurement time-series or a clean state supersession is now an attribute_collision. A `kind` field was probed against the live model (evals/shape_probe.py, `fields` suite, gpt-oss-120b, 12 samples an arm): described with its six words in an imperative 'copy exactly ONE of these six words, and never any other word', it came back legal 7 times in 80 - the model writes the fact's TOPIC (`residence` x15, `employment` x10, `medical` x9, `weight` x5) - and 12 in 85 on the full eleven-field surface. Required buys presence, not membership. The route that does work is the one `_fact_kind` already reads: DECLARE the predicate in `src/jbrain/schema/defs/`, where a declared `kind` wins over the subject type's default. That is registry work under ENTITY_GRAPH_REFOCUS_PLAN's tier-1, not tool work. The one enum-free shape that CAN carry a closed vocabulary was tried too and fails the other way round: a `reading` BOOLEAN (is this a number off an instrument?) came back legal 96 times in 96 and `true` 88 of them - on 'Dana still works at Everlane' and 'I finally sold the Civic' alike - so wiring it would make nearly every fact a measurement, which accumulates and never supersedes. The mirror image of the `negated` boolean, which never fires at all. W5 MUST NOT DELETE: `_fact_kind`, the registry's per-predicate `kind` declaration, or the `attribute_collision` card - it is the only thing standing between an undeclared measurement and a silent overwrite. (2) ACCEPTED, on measurement. assert_fact has no `qualifier` field, so two scalar facts that shared a predicate and differed only in their qualifier collide on one identity key. (Where the qualifier named the OBJECT entity nothing is lost - a non-functional predicate keys on its object.) A `qualifier` field was probed against the live model (evals/shape_probe.py, 12 samples): it filled with prose on 61 of 86 facts - 'previous weight 182 lb in March', 'vehicle no longer owned', 'diagnosed by Dr. Patel' - and left it blank 5 times. An over-applied qualifier SPLITS an identity key, so nothing supersedes ever again; that is strictly worse than the collision it was meant to fix. What ships instead is the channel `registry.decompose_predicate` already read and assert_fact v3 now teaches - `name.nickname.friends` stores as name.nickname + friends - bounded to the five registry predicates declaring a `qualifier_vocab`. A LONG-TAIL qualifier like this one has no such declaration and is still dropped. W5 MUST NOT DELETE: `facts.qualifier`, the identity key that includes it, or `decompose_predicate` and the `qualifier_vocab` declarations it reads. The three readings here differ only in their qualifier (deep/nullval/flat), so they collide on one key. (3) ACCEPTED as designed, not open. `assert_fact.object` is a plain STRING and there is no structured `value_json` field: TOOL_SURFACE gap 5's deliberate narrowing, the model is never asked to nest. So a literal is stored as {value} or {value, unit} and anything richer is flattened by runner._object_literal first, while an edge with an object entity stores no value_json at all. W5 MUST NOT DELETE: `facts.value_json`, `_quantity_value`'s unit split, or `supersession.values_equal`'s cross-unit comparison - the EMR importer and the projections write and read structured values through the non-model path. The nested payload and the 13-key flat object are flattened by runner._object_literal to '0 1 2 ... 12' and stored as {value: '...'} - which is precisely the robustness property this scenario exists to pin, so it cannot be tested through this surface at all.
